analysis.title: FirstEnergy Corp. (FE): Raising estimates on transmission upside, further opportunity in WV; Buy
key_insights: GS raises FE estimates after 3Q26 results. EPS CAGR through 2030 is now 8.6%, up from 8.0%, driven by higher transmission capex revenue.

FE expects transmission investment to rise at least 25% versus its current $19bn 2026-30 plan as it rolls forward to 2027-31. Management said most of the increase comes from broader reliability and resiliency needs, not data centers.
Management still assumes about $250mn of transmission investment per 1 GW of contracted load. Contracted data center demand rose to 7.9 GW, with about 4 GW more in active negotiations.
GS raises 2027-30 transmission capex estimates by about $3.5bn, adding EPS upside of 1% in 2028, 2% in 2029 and 2% in 2030.
Maidsville (West Virginia generation) is the next key catalyst. A CPCN decision is expected in 4Q26 and FE has reserved turbines for delivery in 2030.

FE is in discussions on another 3 GW of potential load in WV and has issued an RFP for 3 GW of additional CCGT equipment, with longer-term generation expected in 2031-32 and beyond. Bridge power options could bring customers online as soon as 2028, and FE is weighing both rate-based and GenCo structures.
WV rate case resolved: $76mn Inflation and Investment Adjustment approved as filed, first increase effective August 1, 2026 and second on June 1, 2027, with a stay-out through April 2028.
Ohio 3-Year Rate Plan: staff report due November 30, 2026 and hearings begin March 2027.

New Jersey $253mn base rate case is underway, reflecting about $1bn of rate base growth since the February 2024 increase. FE proposes delaying the bill impact until 2028, and a state affordability review may give clarity late this year or early next.
Maryland: FE filed for a $53mn revenue increase in September, with hearings in January 2027 and an outcome expected April 2027.
GS cuts nothing but raises 12-month PT to $55 from $53, based on an unchanged 17.5x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates, a 1x premium over baseline. FE trades at a 6% P/E discount to GS coverage (ex CA).

market_movers.rationale: PT raised from $53 on higher transmission capex and EPS estimates. Shares at $46.83 imply 17.4% upside, with a Maidsville CPCN decision expected in 4Q26 as the next catalyst.

sector_views.rationale: GS has a Buy on FE, citing transmission growth, data center demand and regulatory progress. The report gives no broad sector stance.

earnings_insights: FE 3Q26 results reported before this note (30 Oct 2026). GS updated its model for 3Q26 actuals. The 3Q26 EPS figure is shown as $0.98 in the quarterly table under the 9/26 column, which the report does not label as reported or estimate.
GS revenue estimates (GS forecast) for 2026E/2027E/2028E are $16,459mn/$17,625.3mn/$18,512.1mn, from $16,194.1mn/$17,408.6mn/$18,255.2mn. 2025 revenue was $15,079mn and 2025 EPS was $2.55.
Contracted data center demand rose to 7.9 GW from the prior level, with about 4 GW more in active negotiations.
risk_factors: Unfavorable outcome from the Ohio rate case.
Pension expense and/or interest expense higher than expected.
